checks: Recomputed optically thin disk Tb_RJ(258 GHz) for S=255 mJy: 47/21/12/5 mK for FWHM 10/15/20/30" (matches q38_jbg). The log's Tb_RJ(10.5" beam) values differ only by beam dilution, as expected.

q38_jbg grid is internally consistent: Tbg_eq is monotonic in F, eta, beta and Td. Worst case (Td=25, beta=1.5, F=10", eta=1) gives 2.76/2.89/3.23/3.89 K, so the envelope stays below ~4 K and is mostly ~2.7-3.2 K. This lies inside the q36 'envhi' scenario already run for Q22, so skipping a new Q22 run is justified.

Recovered 35-70 mJy vs predicted 140-690 mJy global dust: consistent with a lower-limit interpretation; the global FIR flux is an upper envelope for the 10" region because it includes the whole merger, which makes the bound conservative.

MRS values are inferred from beam size and the handbook formula, not from visibilities. This is stated honestly and does not change the conclusion, since any smooth disk of >~10-15" is resolved out in all configurations considered.
notes_for_questioner: 1) Get the actual MRS and shortest baselines from listobs of the Band 5/6/7 MSs, and check whether any ACA/7m data exist for NGC 3256 (Band 6/7 ACA would directly recover the extended dust). 2) The disk FWHM is the main unknown; Herschel 70/160/250 um maps or APEX/LABOCA 870 um could fix it. 3) Publish the Q38 result as a short addendum to p0046 stating the envelope Tbg_eq <~3.2 K (<=3.9 K at 4-3 in the extreme case) and that a hot envelope is neither required nor excluded. 4) The decisive discriminator remains an independent envelope temperature tracer.
